title: Chaitanya by the river: bhakti's ladder
hookLine: by a river, a renunciant asks a governor to teach him, and keeps saying: say more
carry: bhakti is a ladder: always one rung further
tomorrow: what tears a garden of devotion up by the roots?

lines: THE RENUNCIANT ASKS TO BE TAUGHT.
cards: Some conversations go deeper every time someone says: and? This one happens by the Godavari river, and the roles are upside down. Chaitanya is the renunciant, the one who left the world.
Ramananda Raya is a governor, a householder, a man of the world. And it's the renunciant who asks the householder to teach. Ramananda hesitates.
Chaitanya answers with a line the Charitamrita keeps: whoever knows the truth of Krishna is a teacher, whatever their birth, whether they've left home or not. So Ramananda begins.
And every answer he gives gets the same reply.

teach.h: THAT'S ON THE OUTSIDE. SAY MORE.
teach.b: Chaitanya asks: tell me the goal.
Ramananda starts with duty: doing the work that's yours brings devotion to Vishnu. Chaitanya's reply becomes the refrain of the whole talk: that's on the outside; say more. Ramananda tries again.
Offering the fruit of your work to Krishna. On the outside. Giving up your duties.
Still outside. Devotion mixed with knowledge. Outside.
Then Ramananda names a devotion that doesn't lean on knowledge at all, simple loving service. This time Chaitanya says: yes, that's so. Now go further.
And the talk climbs. To prema, love itself.
Then love for Krishna as a servant loves, then as a friend, then as a parent, then as a beloved. And at the top, Radha's love. That's why he keeps saying more.
It's a ladder, and Chaitanya keeps asking for the next rung.

This is a teaching Gaudiya Vaishnavas still build on: love for Krishna grows by stages, and it can take the shape of any close bond, a servant's, a friend's, a parent's, a beloved's. Notice where the ladder starts.
Duty and offered work, the heart of last week's karma, aren't thrown away; the talk calls them a first step.
That's the Charitamrita's ladder, and Gaudiya Vaishnavas still teach from it; other Hindu schools order these paths their own way.
And the book never forgets where it happened: a householder by a river, teaching the renunciant who asked.

how: Gaudiya Vaishnava teachers use the conversation with Ramananda Raya to lay out devotion in stages, from duty and offered work to love as servant, friend, parent and beloved.

o: a duty to work that leaves no room for love
devotion as a ladder: always a further rung
a knowledge that replaces the love of God

games.q: by the river — tap the pairs.
p: a governor and householder who teaches

s: in this talk, duty and work are thrown out as worthless
they're called outside, a first step, and the talk climbs from there.
Chaitanya, the renunciant, asks the householder to teach him
whoever knows the truth of Krishna is a teacher, he says.
the ladder ends at knowledge of the self
it climbs through love as servant, friend, parent and beloved, up to Radha's love.

games.q: a friend says real devotion means quitting school and leaving home like a monk; people with jobs and families can't really go far. what does the scene by the Godavari say?
o: a householder taught the monk there: whoever knows Krishna's truth can teach, home or not.
she's right: only renunciants climb the higher rungs.
devotion is for later, after work and family are done.
games.why: Chaitanya, the renunciant, sat down to learn from Ramananda, a governor with a household: whoever knows the truth of Krishna is a teacher, whatever their station. and duty, offered to Krishna, is the ladder's first rung.

practice: If you know a bhajan, a kirtan line, or simply Krishna's name, sing or say one line softly. Then say it again, slower, with a little more of yourself in it, the way Chaitanya kept asking for more.
Three or four times, one rung further each time. If you don't pray, hum a tune you love and listen a little further into it each time.

wordCard.voice: Bhakti: devotion, here a ladder. Every answer is good, and there's always a further rung.

orig.note: Sanskrit prema, love; in Ramananda's answers, the rung after loving service, from which the ladder climbs to Radha's love.

carryVoice: Your line: bhakti is a ladder, always one rung further. Ramananda climbed it by the Godavari. Day three of the book.

sources.ref: Chaitanya Charitamrita, Madhya-lila 8 (the meeting with Ramananda Raya on the Godavari; whoever knows the truth of Krishna is a guru, whether brahmin, renunciant or shudra; the questions on the goal and the refrain 'this is external, say more'; devotion free of knowledge accepted, then prema, servitude, friendship, parental love, conjugal love, and Radha's love)
